title: Host Accounts Programme Rules: Assignment of the Host Tier
content:
# Host Programme Rules — Assignment of the Host Tier

These rules govern which host tier a Host Accounts holder sits in. The figures they name (live-listing counts, ratings, account age and completed stays) are the thresholds published for the tiers of Host Accounts.

## 1. Tiers and their conditions

1.1 **Retired wording.** The clause "the tier of a host account is decided in this order of precedence, the first that applies winning" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis of Host Accounts.

1.2 **Enterprise Partner** is the tier of an account with a signed partner agreement and at least the Enterprise Partner live-listing threshold of live listings.

1.3 **Retired wording.** The clause placing in Professional Host Plus an account with at least the Professional Host Plus live-listing threshold and an average guest rating of at least the Professional Host Plus rating threshold is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis of Host Accounts.

1.4 **Professional Host** is the tier of an account with a business name, or with at least the Professional Host live-listing threshold of live listings.

1.5 **Individual accounts** sit in Superhost, Standard Host or Starter Host.

## 2. Leaving Starter Host

A Starter Host becomes a Standard Host once the account is at least the Starter Host graduation age old and has the Starter Host graduation number of completed stays. Both conditions are needed together.

## 3. Superhost assessments

3.1 Individual Standard Hosts and Superhosts are assessed on the Superhost assessment dates, over the Superhost lookback period.

3.2 **Retired wording.** The clause stating that the assessment is met when the average rating, the response rate recorded by the messaging system, the cancellation rate and the completed stays or completed nights reach the Superhost standards is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis of Host Accounts.

3.3 A met assessment promotes a Standard Host to Superhost; a not-met assessment demotes a Superhost to Standard Host; otherwise the tier is unchanged.

| Tier before the assessment | Outcome | Tier after |
|---|---|---|
| Standard Host | Met | Superhost (promoted) |
| Superhost | Not met | Standard Host (demoted) |
| Standard Host | Not met | Standard Host (unchanged) |
| Superhost | Met | Superhost (unchanged) |

3.4 Superhost is lost at once on suspension where the tier's terms provide that a suspension removes Superhost status.

## 4. Effect of a tier change on booked stays

4.1 **Retired wording.** The clause "a tier change applies to stays booked after it" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis of Host Accounts.

4.2 Stays already booked keep the fee structure frozen on them.

superseded_clauses: The tier of a host account is decided in this order of precedence, the first that applies winning
Professional Host Plus for an account with at least professional_plus_min_live_listings live listings and an average guest rating of at least professional_plus_min_avg_rating

the assessment is met when the average rating (host_msr_avg_rating_365d) is at least superhost_min_avg_rating, the response rate recorded by the messaging system is at least superhost_min_response_rate_pct, the cancellation rate (host_msr_cancellation_rate_365d) is below superhost_max_cancellation_rate_pct, and either completed stays (host_msr_completed_stays_365d) reach superhost_min_stays_12m or completed stays reach superhost_alt_min_stays_12m with completed nights (host_msr_completed_nights_365d) reaching superhost_alt_min_nights_12m
A tier change applies to stays booked after it
